> [!NOTE]
> This repository hosts the **public dashboard** of economic activity in **Mauritius** measured with night-time lights seen from space (2014–2025). The site is bilingual (English / French), fully static and regenerated each time the notebook runs.

## 💡 Key messages

1. **National trend** — Between 2014 and 2025, night-time light in Mauritius changed by +6.1% per year (95% CI: +4.2% to +7.5%). Over the last 12 months, the seasonally adjusted level is -6.1% relative to the previous 12 months.  
   <sub>🟢 high · significant trend (p < 0.01; n = 12)</sub>
2. **Regions** — Of 12 ADM2 units, 10 show significant growth, 1 are stagnating and 0 are declining. Light remains concentrated: Plaines Wilhems accounts for 20% of national light.  
   <sub>🟠 medium · classification of 12 units, threshold ±1%/yr and p < 0.10</sub>
3. **Convergence** — Across ADM2 units, light per capita shows neither statistically established convergence nor divergence.  
   <sub>🔴 low · β = −0.015 [−0.048; 0.017], n = 10</sub>
4. **Link with GDP** — The elasticity of light with respect to real GDP is 0.88 in levels (95% CI: 0.22 to 1.54, R² = 0.84, 12 years) and 0.27 in growth rates (CI: 0.04 to 0.50). In pseudo-real time (each year predicted from earlier years only), light growth tracks GDP growth with a correlation of −0.09 (mean absolute error: 5.6 percentage points of growth, better than the best naive forecast, error ratio 0.95).  
   <sub>🟠 medium · n = 12, significant but wide CI (1.32)</sub>
5. **Shocks** — The most pronounced shock in the seasonally adjusted series is “COVID-19”: trough of -2.4% (10/2021), return to the pre-shock level after 20 months.  
   <sub>🔴 low · trough compared with pre-shock month-to-month variability</sub>
6. **Inequality and access** — The Gini coefficient of light per capita (ADM2) is 0.21 in 2025 (no significant change since 2014). About 0.01 million people live in inhabited areas with no detectable light (0% of the inhabited population).  
   <sub>🟠 medium · sensitive to the radiance threshold (from 0.00 to 0.03 M depending on the threshold); a proxy for outdoor lighting, not for grid connection</sub>
7. **Industrial zones** — 9 candidate industrial zones are detected (3 major hubs, 0 energy sites), covering 9 km². They emit 6% of national light; the largest is Port Louis (Port Louis). Their light changes by +0.9% per year.  
   <sub>🔴 low · candidate zones, not validated against OpenStreetMap</sub>

## 🛰️ Day and night

The country's main economic pole (Plaines Wilhems (Plaines Wilhems)), by day as seen by Sentinel-2 and by night as seen by VIIRS. What the satellite sees at night — the lighting of cities, ports, factories and roads — is the proxy of activity used throughout this project.

## 🏭 Industrial zones

<p align="center"><img src="docs/img/industry.png" alt="industry" width="80%"></p>

Industrial sites shine at night like towns, but their buildings are mostly non-residential, few people live there and they emit NO₂. Combining VIIRS, GHSL (non-residential built-up, population) and Sentinel-5P, **9 candidate zones** are detected; they emit **6%** of national light. 

| # | Zone | Type | Area | Share of national light | Growth / yr |
|---:|---|---|---:|---:|---:|
| 1 | Port Louis (Port Louis) | Major industrial hub | 3.6 km² | 3.8% | -0.5% |
| 2 | Black River (Black River) | Major industrial hub | 1.2 km² | 0.4% | +7.7% |
| 3 | Moka (Moka) | Major industrial hub | 0.6 km² | 0.4% | +8.0% |
| 4 | Black River (Black River) | Industrial / logistics zone | 0.8 km² | 0.3% | -0.7% |
| 5 | Plaines Wilhems (Plaines Wilhems) | Industrial / logistics zone | 0.8 km² | 0.3% | +3.7% |
| 6 | Pamplemousses (Pamplemousses) | Industrial / logistics zone | 0.8 km² | 0.2% | +10.3% |
| 7 | Pamplemousses (Pamplemousses) | Industrial / logistics zone | 0.4 km² | 0.1% | -5.0% |
| 8 | Grand Port (Grand Port) | Industrial / logistics zone | 0.4 km² | 0.1% | -1.2% |

## ⚙️ How it is computed

Processing chain run on Google Earth Engine from the *Night-time lights and economic activity* notebook (part 3):

```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["🛰️ VIIRS DNB monthly<br/>and annual (VNL V2)"] --> B["🧹 Cleaning<br/>clouds · gas flares · background"]
    B --> C["🗺️ Zonal statistics<br/>country · regions · districts"]
    P["👥 GHSL population<br/>🏭 non-residential built-up<br/>💨 Sentinel-5P NO₂"] --> C
    C --> D["📈 Series, trends,<br/>shocks, breaks"]
    C --> E["⚖️ Inequality,<br/>people in the dark"]
    C --> F["🏭 Industrial zones"]
    W["🏦 World Bank<br/>GDP · electricity access"] --> G["💹 Light–GDP<br/>elasticity"]
    C --> G
    D & E & F & G --> H["🌍 Bilingual dashboard<br/>GitHub Pages"]
    classDef default fill:#E8F5EF,stroke:#00704A,color:#231F20;
    class H fill:#00704A,color:#fff,stroke:#F5C242
```

<details>
<summary><b>The six analyses in detail</b></summary>


| | |
|---|---|
| **📈 Time dynamics** | STL decomposition, year-on-year change, Theil–Sen trend with Mann–Kendall test, anomalies, breaks |
| **🗺️ Regional growth** | Growth / Stagnation / Decline classes (Benjamini–Hochberg correction), HHI, β and σ convergence |
| **💹 Lights and GDP** | elasticity (HAC errors, bootstrap), nowcast judged against two naive forecasts, experimental regional GDP |
| **⚡ Shocks** | trough, gap vs trend, months to recovery, placebo test, Black Marble daily index |
| **⚖️ Inequality and access** | Gini, Theil (between / within regions), urban / rural ratio, people in the dark at three thresholds |
| **🏭 Industrial zones** | four-signal score (light, non-residential built-up, low density, NO₂), OpenStreetMap validation |

</details>

## ⚠️ Limitations to keep in mind

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Lights measure radiance at about 1:30 a.m., not value added. Keep in mind:
>
> - **Blooming and saturation** — light spills beyond built-up areas; the brightest cores plateau
> - **Gas flares** — bright without local activity: masked, but worth watching
> - **Seasonality** — clouds, fires and vegetation create non-economic cycles
> - **Sensor breaks** — DMSP → VIIRS, VNL V2.1 → V2.2: handled with dummies, not eliminated
> - **Rural areas** — the signal is weakest where the rural poor live
> - **Status** — experimental estimates, not official statistics

## 🔁 Reproduce or adapt to another country

The site is produced by the **Night-time lights and economic activity** notebook (part 3) (Colab). Changing the `ISO3` code in the parameters cell is enough to analyse another country; sections 12 and 13 export and re-publish this repository.
